title: Hua Hin Vineyard 2026 — Monsoon Valley Wine, Cycling & How to Get There | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Full guide to Monsoon Valley Vineyard near Hua Hin, Thailand: wine tasting sets, cycling through the vines, The Sala restaurant with mountain views, prices, and how to get there from town.
keywords: Hua Hin vineyard, Monsoon Valley, Hua Hin wine tasting, vineyard cycling Thailand, Hua Hin Hills Vineyard
intro: About 35 kilometres inland from Hua Hin beach, tucked into a valley ringed by hills, sits a vineyard that has been making serious tropical wine for years. This isn't just a photo stop — you can cycle along the rows of vines, taste wines by the flight, and settle in for a long afternoon lunch looking out over the vineyard. We've pulled together the prices, opening hours, and the real ways to get there, all on one page.

blocks.html: The official name is Monsoon Valley Vineyard (people still often call it Hua Hin Hills Vineyard). It belongs to Siam Winery and sits in Nong Phlap, in the hills behind Hua Hin town. The draw is the vineyard-in-the-mountains setting that's genuinely rare in Thailand, plus the chance to try wine actually grown and made in the tropics. If you assumed Thai wine couldn't be done well, this is the place that changes your mind.

Entry to the vineyard is free — there's no gate fee. You only pay for what you choose to do, whether that's renting a bike, a tasting flight, or a meal at the restaurant. It works for couples, families, and groups of friends who want to escape the beach and chill somewhere with a different feel.
There are really three main things to do: taste wine, cycle, and sit back with a drink and a view. Pick one or do all three — most people spend around half a day here.

items: Wine tasting — order a flight and compare several wines in one go. There are wine-only sets and sets paired with tapas.
Cycling in the vineyard — there are routes along the rows of vines and around the lake; just rent a bike at the service point.
Vineyard and mountain views — walk up to the viewpoint or sit at the restaurant and watch the vines stretch out to the hills. The light is gorgeous in the late afternoon.
Wine bottle painting — decorate your own bottle to take home as a souvenir, fun if you've got kids or a group of friends along.

blocks.text: Wine tasting — which flight to order

blocks.html: The thing a lot of people come for is the tasting flight. The nice part is you get to try several wines without paying for a full bottle. The popular one is the premium three-wine flight (Colombard white, Shiraz red, and White Shiraz) for around 290 THB. If you want something to nibble on alongside, there are wine-and-tapas sets too.

items.name: Premium 3-wine flight
items.blurb: Covers white, red, and rosé in a single flight — ideal for a first visit when you just want to know what Thai wine tastes like. Best value if you're on your own.

items.name: Wine-only flights (various)
items.blurb: Several flights to choose from depending on how many wines and which labels, from a small set up to one that includes the special-edition bottles. Good if you're serious about comparing.

items.name: Wine + tapas set
items.blurb: Pairs the wine with snacks like cheese and tapas — easier to linger over and more filling. Great if you're coming as a couple or a group.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Tasting prices and the wine list change with the season and stock, so check the menu at the counter or ask before ordering to be sure. And if you've driven yourself, remember that once you've been tasting you'll want a non-drinking driver, or take the shuttle instead.

Another favourite is renting a bike and riding along the rows of vines — the cool breeze in the valley is just right. There's an easy route of about 3 kilometres for most people, and a tougher "red" route of around 4 kilometres for stronger riders. Rental starts at around 100 THB for 30 minutes and 150 THB for 1 hour.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Ride in the morning or evening when it's more comfortable — midday sun in the valley is fairly strong. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and water with you.

blocks.text: The Sala — dining with vineyard views

blocks.html: On the grounds is The Sala Wine Bar & Bistro, an open-sided pavilion that looks out over the vines running all the way to the hills. It's where people settle in for a while to eat, sip wine, and take photos. The menu has both Western and Thai dishes to go with the estate's own wines.

items.name: A table with vineyard views
items.blurb: Tables along the terrace look out over the rows of vines and the hills, and the light is at its best in the evening. Booking ahead is worth it, especially on weekends.

items.name: A glass and a chill
items.blurb: Order a single glass with a snack and just relax — perfect if you don't want a big meal but want to soak up the atmosphere.

blocks.html: The vineyard and The Sala are open daily, with hours that shift by season. From April to October they're open 9:00–19:00 (last orders 18:30), and from November to March 9:00–20:00 (last orders 19:30). Aim to arrive in the late afternoon and stay through sunset for the best atmosphere.

blocks.text: How to get there from Hua Hin

blocks.html: The vineyard is in Nong Phlap, about 35 kilometres from Hua Hin town, up into the valley. There's no public transport that goes all the way there, so there are three main options.

items: Drive / rent a car — the most convenient and flexible, around 40–50 minutes from town, with parking on site. Best if you've got a non-drinking driver.

Taxi / private car — book a taxi or hire a car for the round trip with waiting time, good for groups who want to taste wine without driving. Agree on a total price including the wait with the driver before you set off.
Vineyard shuttle — there's a shuttle service from a meeting point at Villa Market in Hua Hin, around 300 THB per person round trip. Book ahead, since the departures are limited.

blocks.title: Plan ahead
blocks.html: If you're set on eating at The Sala or using the shuttle, call or email to book in advance — especially on Saturdays and Sundays and through the cool season when it gets busy. Reserving keeps you from missing out.

The vineyard looks its best from late rainy season into the cool season (roughly November–February), when the weather is pleasant, the vines are green, and it's close to harvest. As for the time of day, late afternoon into evening is when the light is loveliest and the air is just right. If you can, come on a weekday — it's far less crowded than weekends.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Monsoon Valley Vineyard?
faq.a: Entry is free — there's no gate fee. You only pay for what you do, such as bike rental from around 100 THB, a tasting flight from around 240–290 THB, or a meal at The Sala depending on what you order.

faq.q: How do you get to the Hua Hin vineyard without a car?
faq.a: The vineyard runs a shuttle from a meeting point at Villa Market in Hua Hin, around 300 THB per person round trip — book ahead, as departures are limited. Alternatively, hire a taxi for the round trip with waiting time; just agree on a total price including the wait with the driver before you leave.

faq.q: How far is the Hua Hin vineyard from town?
faq.a: It's in Nong Phlap, about 35 kilometres from Hua Hin town, up into the valley. Driving takes around 40–50 minutes.

faq.q: Roughly how much is wine tasting at the vineyard?
faq.a: The premium three-wine flight is around 290 THB, other wine-only flights run around 240–735 THB, and wine-and-tapas sets start at around 400 THB. Prices change with the season and the wine list, so check the menu at the counter before ordering.

faq.q: What's the best time to visit the Hua Hin vineyard?
faq.a: November–February brings cool weather, green vines, and the lead-up to harvest. For the time of day, aim for late afternoon into evening when the light is best and the air is comfortable. Avoiding weekends means smaller crowds.
